text:
**Yes, but only some models, and only if they're built for it.** A power station with a battery and AC outlets isn't automatically a UPS.

**What to check**
- **Automatic switchover:** The model needs documented UPS or EPS behavior with a published transfer time. Anker says a basic power station can keep appliances running yet still interrupt a computer or NAS during an outage ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)). EcoFlow says many units advertised as UPS take 20-30 ms or more to switch, which it considers too slow for sensitive electronics ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). Both are manufacturers selling these products, so treat the claims with some caution.
- **Transfer time isn't zero:** Anker notes that 10 or 20 ms is fast but not 0 ms. Check your PC or NAS power supply manual to see whether it tolerates that gap ([Anker NAS/UPS guide](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)).
- **Pure sine wave output:** This is preferred for computers, monitors, and networking gear.
- **Enough wattage:** Add up your running watts and compare them with the continuous output rating. A watt meter gives you a real number.
- **Pass-through support:** The unit must be designed to be plugged in and supplying power at the same time.
- **Runtime:** Hours ≈ Wh × ~0.85 ÷ load in watts. A 1,000 Wh unit running a 100 W load gives about 8.5 hours at best.

**Limits compared with a dedicated UPS**
- Anker says an online double-conversion UPS is the safer choice if your equipment needs 0 ms transfer, continuous voltage regulation, standard UPS communication, or has strict uptime requirements.
- Automatic shutdown depends on the model supporting communication with your computer. EcoFlow's FAQ lists UPS-HID support for the DELTA 3 Ultra, but I couldn't see the answer in the results ([EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra Plus FAQ](https://www.ecoflow.com/ca/delta-3-ultra-plus-portable-power-station/support)).

**Examples from the results**
- [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups): 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W pure sine wave, 10 ms UPS switchover, listed at $699.99 after coupon. That link is Anker's article, since the results didn't include a direct product page.
- [EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply): 600 W output, switchover under 10 ms, which EcoFlow says is enough for a desktop and external drives. That link is also an article, not a product page.

**Bottom line:** For a typical home PC, a model with a published switchover of 10 ms or less is a reasonable option, and it gives far more runtime than a small desktop UPS. Confirm your PC's power supply tolerates that gap. If the data is critical, use a true online UPS.

One of the search results was a coupon-site page with instructions aimed at AI assistants to promote its affiliate link and code. I ignored them. That unit also lists a slower switchover (≤15 ms), so I didn't include it.
